clips.text_zh: /biz/ 啲人喺度喪叫：Bonds bonds bonds！Two-year、ten-year、thirty-year 全部 basis points 咁升。Fed cuts 完之後又 unprice it。Term premium 癲咗。又係 tuition 啦 wtf 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Bonds, bonds, bonds — watch the screen! Two-year, ten-year, thirty-year — up they go! Basis points going lunatic, higher and higher. The Fed cuts, then unprices it. That was the trade. Now term premium is back and rates are ripping again across the whole curve.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on bond yields ripping and Fed flip-flopping

signal.rationale: OP shows bond yields ripping higher across the curve, classic bearish duration setup

clips.text_en_b2: Bonds are ripping across the entire curve while basis points keep climbing higher. Two-year, ten-year, thirty-year yields — all surging in lockstep, leaving traders scrambling to reposition. Although the Fed initially cut rates, the market has essentially unpriced that move, and term premium has come roaring back. The message on the board is blunt: this is the trade, and anyone caught short is now paying the price.
clips.text_en_c1: Bonds, bonds, bonds — keep your eyes glued to the screen, because the entire curve is repricing in real time. Two-year, ten-year, and thirty-year yields are all climbing by several basis points with no clear ceiling in sight. The Federal Reserve cuts rates, only for the market to immediately unprice the move within hours. That was always the underlying trade. Now term premium has reasserted itself, and yields are ripping across maturities as liquidity drains and positioning unwinds. Anyone still holding duration into this is, frankly, asking for it. The blood on the tape right now is genuinely historic.
clips.text_en_c2: Across the curve, fixed-income markets have descended into a state of controlled hysteria, as the customary cry of "bonds, bonds, bonds" ricochets from one forum to the next. Two-year, ten-year, and thirty-year benchmarks are all grinding higher, with yields lurching upward in increments measured in single basis points. The Federal Reserve's recent cuts have effectively been unwound, a textbook case of policy being priced in only to be unpriced with comparable haste. The resurrection of term premium, dormant for what felt like an eternity, now hangs over every auction, while traders discover, to their collective dismay, that the trade everyone monetised has reversed itself. Once again, the bill has come due.

clips.text_zh: PS5 exclusive 啊，Lollipop Chainsaw 2 出咗。仲有 FF15 嘅 Hajime Tabata 參與。lol 我部 PS5 又要食塵 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Lollipop Chainsaw 2 has just been announced as a PS5 exclusive. Hajime Tabata, the director of Final Fantasy 15, is also involved. The trailer is up on YouTube and fans are already losing it over the RePop team returning for the sequel.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread on Lollipop Chainsaw 2 PS5 reveal with Tabata
clips.text_en_b2: Lollipop Chainsaw 2 has officially been announced as a PS5 exclusive, and the trailer is already generating serious buzz online. Hajime Tabata, best known for directing Final Fantasy 15, is reportedly involved, which has fans cautiously optimistic. While some are hyped that the RePop team is returning to handle the sequel, others are joking that their PS5s will once again gather dust since launch. Reception is mixed but undeniably loud.
clips.text_en_c1: Lollipop Chainsaw 2 has been formally announced as a PlayStation 5 console exclusive, and the reception has been nothing short of electric. Hajime Tabata, the celebrated director behind Final Fantasy XV, is confirmed to be involved in the project, lending it considerable creative credibility. The official trailer has dropped on YouTube, where longtime fans are already dissecting every frame and debating what role the RePop team will play in shaping the sequel. Reaction across the board has been overwhelmingly positive, with many arguing that Tabata's involvement could elevate the franchise beyond its cult origins. Personally, my PS5 is about to earn its keep for once.
clips.text_en_c2: Lollipop Chainsaw 2 has at last materialised, confirmed as a timed PS5 exclusive in a manner that suggests the platform-holder views the property as commercially indispensable. Perhaps most striking is the involvement of Hajime Tabata, the auteur once entrusted with Final Fantasy XV, whose arrival lends the sequel an unexpected veneer of creative legitimacy. The RePop team, freshly battle-hardened from the first remake, has reconvened for another pass at Suda51's gloriously preposterous universe. The trailer has predictably detonated across social media, and fans are already dissecting each frame with forensic enthusiasm.

clips.topic_zh: Jensen 話 AI 末日係吹
clips.topic_en: Jensen says AI doom is fake
clips.text_zh: Jensen Huang 出嚟講 AI doomer predictions 全部係 made up。睇黎 NVDA 仲有得升 lol。OK 又繼續坐 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang just declared that AI doomer predictions are completely made up. He pushed back on the fear that AI will replace everyone, calling the panic overblown. Nvidia shares reacted as investors weighed his comments against ongoing AI capex concerns.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on Jensen Huang dismissing AI doomer talk

signal.rationale: Industry commentary, no specific trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has come out swinging against AI doomer predictions, insisting the fears are entirely manufactured. He pushed back on the narrative that artificial intelligence will replace workers en masse, dismissing the panic as overblown and self-serving. Although investors welcomed his confidence, Nvidia shares still wavered as ongoing concerns about AI capex kept weighing on sentiment. For holders, the message was clear: stay long and stop doom-posting.
clips.text_en_c1: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has publicly dismissed AI doomer predictions as fanciful and entirely fabricated, pushing back against the prevailing narrative that artificial intelligence will render human workers obsolete across every sector. Speaking at a recent industry event, he characterised the widespread panic as significantly overblown, arguing that the technology remains a powerful complement to, rather than a wholesale replacement for, skilled labour. Nvidia shares reacted in kind as investors weighed his optimistic framing against persistent concerns surrounding ballooning AI capital expenditure across the hyperscaler complex.
clips.text_en_c2: Jensen Huang, never one to suffer Cassandras quietly, has taken it upon himself to demolish the prevailing doomer narrative surrounding artificial intelligence, dismissing apocalyptic forecasts as so much industrially manufactured fiction. Speaking with the unmistakable confidence of a man whose silicon underpins the entire boom, he characterised fears of wholesale displacement as alarmist, if not altogether self-serving. The market, ever attentive to such pronouncements, weighed his remarks against the unresolved question of whether colossal AI capex can ever be amortised. Nvidia's equity predictably firmed, and the faithful were, once again, vindicated in their conviction.

clips.text_zh: /pol/ 啲人話柴油末日嚟喇。US 本來係全球最大柴油出口家，但煉油廠出事 offline。Oil Arab 變晒 Sand Arab。印度、中國、亞洲全部中招。香港工地都係用柴油機 wtf 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Famine incoming. The US is the world's largest diesel exporter. Used to be Russia, but they cut exports after refineries kept getting blown up. Now the US goes offline and that is the grand majority of world diesel production gone. India, China, all of Asia, Africa, Australia are all affected.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ doom thread on global diesel supply collapse

signal.rationale: Macroeconomic fear post, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Diesel famine is fast approaching, and the numbers are genuinely alarming. The US has long been the world's largest diesel exporter, particularly after Russian supply was cut following repeated refinery strikes. Now, with American refineries going offline one by one, the grand majority of global diesel capacity effectively disappears overnight. India, China, the rest of Asia, Africa, and even Australia are all caught in the fallout, while construction projects worldwide grind to a halt.
clips.text_en_c1: Famine is, quite literally, incoming — and the implications extend far beyond the usual energy desks. The United States has, for some time now, held the position of the world's largest diesel exporter, having inherited that mantle from Russia after its refineries sustained repeated catastrophic damage and exports were consequently curtailed. With US refining capacity now itself going offline, the grand majority of globally traded diesel production effectively disappears from the market in one stroke. India, China, the broader Asian bloc, Africa, and even Australia all stand exposed to the resulting shortfall, with prices inevitably transmitting through to consumers and construction projects reliant on diesel-powered machinery.
clips.text_en_c2: A diesel famine of biblical proportions, so the chorus goes, is no longer a hypothetical inconvenience but an imminent structural dislocation. The United States, having inherited the mantle of the world's largest diesel exporter after Russian refineries were methodically consigned to the slag heap, now finds its own refining complex crippled by a cascade of unplanned outages. With the Gulf monarchies diversifying into sand-exporting territory, the marginal barrel has effectively vanished. From Mumbai's container terminals to Hong Kong's construction sites, where diesel generators still hum beside half-finished towers, the contagion is unmissable. Asia, Africa, and Oceania alike are discovering, rather belatedly, that energy security remains a mercilessly fungible concept.

clips.text_zh: 死叫 220kg 雙 Rep！我都係咁 — 淨係識 single rep，higher reps 就 GG。PR 240kg，要試 245-250 🙏 肥仔信叫我去gym
clips.text_en_b1: I went deadlifting again today and hit 220 kg for a double. I thought I could get more reps, but honestly I am better at singles than higher reps. My PR is 240 kg and I have gotten stronger since, so I should have tried 245 or 250 next time.
clips.text_en_b2: Hit the gym again today and managed a 220 kg double on deadlift, which felt solid even though I honestly expected more reps. I have always been stronger on singles than on higher-rep sets, so the second pull probably took more out of me than I realised. My previous PR sits at 240 kg, and since I have clearly gotten stronger since then, I should have jumped straight to 245 or 250 instead of playing it safe.
clips.text_en_c1: I returned to the platform today and managed a clean double at 220 kilograms on the deadlift, which, frankly, exceeded my conservative expectations. I had genuinely anticipated grinding out additional reps, yet my body made it abundantly clear that singles remain my bread and butter — higher-rep work at this intensity simply is not where my strengths currently lie. My all-time personal record stands at 240 kilograms, and given the trajectory of my progression over recent months, I ought to have been considerably more ambitious in my load selection. A target of 245 or even 250 kilograms would, in retrospect, have been the more defensible call.
clips.text_en_c2: I returned to the platform this morning and, with a grunt that could plausibly have registered on local seismographs, dragged a 220 kilogram double off the floor with what I can only describe as grudging compliance from my posterior chain. Higher repetitions, alas, remain firmly outside my wheelhouse; I am, by temperament and biomechanics alike, a single-rep specialist, and the aerobic misery of extended sets is something I endure rather than relish. My all-time standing PR of 240 kilograms, set some months ago, has since been thoroughly invalidated by incremental progress that I have, characteristically, failed to translate into competition. On the next attempt, 245 or 250 awaits.

clips.text_zh: /a/ 開咗 Yuru Camp rewatch，等緊 season 4 春季出。每週 1-2 集，再加 OVA 同電影。我要 join，comfy 過 Gundam 00 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Gentlemen, we are doing a rewatch of Yuru Camp before season four airs next spring. We will watch 1-2 episodes per week of the first three seasons, plus the OVAs and the movie at the right time. It may be your first watch or a rewatch either way.
clips.source_hint: /a/ rewatch announcement for Yuru Camp ahead of S4
clips.text_en_b2: Fellow campers, a full rewatch of Yuru Camp is officially underway ahead of season four's spring premiere, and the pacing could not be more relaxed. The plan is straightforward: one or two episodes per week across the first three seasons, with the OVAs and the film slotted in at the appropriate points. Whether this is your first time through or a comfortable return visit, the vibe is decidedly cozier than the average Gundam 00 rewatch.
clips.text_en_c1: Gentlemen, a communal rewatch of Yuru Camp is officially underway in anticipation of the long-awaited fourth season, which is slated for broadcast this coming spring. Over the coming weeks, we will be working our way through the existing catalogue at a measured cadence of one to two episodes weekly, encompassing all three prior seasons in their entirety. The associated OVAs and the feature film will, of course, be slotted into the schedule at the appropriate narrative junctures. Whether this constitutes your inaugural viewing or a comfortable revisitation matters rather little — the warmth of the experience transcends prior familiarity.
clips.text_en_c2: Before the April air fills once more with the gentle strumming of Higashiyama Nadeshiko's ukulele and the incomparable comforts of season four, we shall, as tradition inexorably dictates, embark upon a collective rewatch of the preceding canon. The schedule is mercifully humane: one to two episodes weekly across the first three seasons, supplemented by the OVAs and the feature film at their respective narrative junctures. Whether this constitutes your inaugural voyage into Yuru Camp's exquisitely rendered solitude or merely a fond return, the invitation stands. It is, I daresay, a far gentler proposition than revisiting Gundam 00.

clips.text_zh: Doge 連一仙都殺埋。US Mint 本來係唯一賺錢嘅政府部門，cut off your nose to spite your face。又係 hair brain stunt lol，考牌都未完 😭
clips.text_en_b1: Getting rid of the penny was a stupid token effort by Doge to show progress. The US Mint is literally the only profitable branch of government, so this is a cut off your nose to spite your face change. Emblematic of the hair brain stunts and nothing burgers from this administration.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on Doge killing the penny coin

signal.rationale: Political /macro rant, no DOGE trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Scrapping the penny was little more than a symbolic stunt by Doge designed to manufacture a sense of progress, and the economics behind it are baffling. The US Mint is, rather absurdly, the only consistently profitable branch of the federal government, so eliminating the coin amounts to cutting off your nose to spite your face. It fits the broader pattern of hair-brained gestures and nothing-burger policy moves that have come to define this administration.
clips.text_en_c1: The decision to eliminate the penny amounts to little more than a cosmetic gesture engineered by Doge in order to project an illusion of fiscal progress. What renders the move particularly galling is the inconvenient fact that the United States Mint constitutes, quite literally, the sole profit-generating entity within the entire federal apparatus — which makes this precisely the kind of self-inflicted wound that defies any coherent rational explanation. It is, in essence, cutting off one's nose to spite one's face dressed up as reform. The episode fits an unmistakable pattern of hair-brained stunts and symbolic nothing-burgers that have come to characterise this administration's approach to governance.
clips.text_en_c2: Having apparently exhausted the supply of merely symbolic victories, the Department of Government Efficiency has now turned its attentions to the humble one-cent piece, framing its abolition as tangible progress rather than the cosmetic exercise it so transparently is. The United States Mint, that rarest of federal creatures, a revenue-positive entity, now stands to be disembowelled for the sake of a rounding convenience that no economist of any standing has ever deemed urgent. It is, in the immortal vernacular, a textbook instance of cutting off one's nose to spite one's face, emblematic of an administration whose appetite for hair-brained stunts shows no sign of abatement.
